question.problem:
In a plumbing store, the length of a water pipe is normally distributed with a mean of $2\,\text{m}$ and a standard deviation of $0.05\,\text{m}.$ If Carl bought $25$ pipes, what is the probability that the total length of the pipes he purchased is more than $49.8\,m$ and less $50.2\,m?$ It can be assumed that the lengths of pipes are mutually independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7580\,$ | $\,0.7611\,$ | $\,0.7642\,$ | $\,0.7673\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7881\,$ | $\,0.7910\,$ | $\,0.7939\,$ | $\,0.7967\,$ |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8159\,$ | $\,0.8186\,$ | $\,0.8212\,$ | $\,0.8238\,$ |

current_example.problem:
In a library, each shelf is filled with $20$ volumes of an encyclopedia, plus one bookend. The weight of one volume, in grams, is normally distributed with a mean of $150\,\textrm g$ and a standard deviation of $5\,\textrm g,$ while the weight of a bookend, in grams, is normally distributed with a mean of $50\,\textrm g$ and a standard deviation of $2\,\textrm g.$ If one shelf is randomly selected, what is the probability that it supports a weight of more than $3\,000\,\textrm g?$ You may assume that the weights of the volumes and bookend are mutually independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $\Phi(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $\Phi(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\, 0.00 \,$ | $\, 0.01 \,$ | $\, 0.02 \,$ | $\, 0.03 \,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\, 2.0 \,$ | $\, 0.9772 \,$ | $\, 0.9778 \,$ | $\, 0.9783 \,$ | $\, 0.9788 \,$ |
| $\, 2.1 \,$ | $\, 0.9821 \,$ | $\, 0.9826 \,$ | $\, 0.9830 \,$ | $\, 0.9834 \,$ |
| $\, 2.2 \,$ | $\, 0.9861 \,$ | $\, 0.9864 \,$ | $\, 0.9868 \,$ | $\, 0.9871 \,$ |
current_example.worked_solution:
Let $X_i$ denote the weight of the $i$th volume, and let $Y$ denote the weight of a bookend. Then, we have

$$
X_i \sim N(150, 5^2), \qquad 1\leq i \leq 20,
$$

and

$$
Y \sim N(50, 2^2).
$$

Let the random variable $W$ denote the weight of a randomly selected shelf. Then, since

$$
W = X_1+X_2+\cdots + X_{20} + Y,
$$

we have that $W$ is normally distributed, where

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[W] & =20\cdot 150+50 \\  & =3\,050, \\ \text{Var}[W] & =20\cdot {5}^{2}+{2}^{2} \\  & =504.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
W \sim N(3\,050, 504).
$$

In order to find $P(W > 3\,000),$ we convert $W$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W>3\,000) & =P(Z>\frac{3\,000-3\,050}{\sqrt{504}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>-2.23) \\  & =P(Z<2.23) \\  & =Φ(2.23)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
\Phi(2.23)\approx 0.9871.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(W>3\,000) & ≈Φ(2.23) \\  & =0.9871.\end{aligned}
$$
